text:
bob_acme: Hey team — our integration with Redwood started failing this morning when we call the `lookup_user` tool. Getting a 400 with 'Malformed tool args: invalid JSON'. Happens intermittently.

alice_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact request body you send (redact tokens)? Also include request id if available.

bob_acme: Here's a minimal repro (redacted):
```
POST /v1/respond HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Find user"}],
  "function_call": {"name":"lookup_user"},
  "tool_args": "{\"user_id\": \"12345\", \"filter\": \"name:\"O'Connor\"\",}"
}
```

bob_acme: The important bit is `tool_args` is a string (we build it from templates) and contains unescaped inner quotes and a trailing comma. Some requests succeed, some fail.

alice_support: Thanks — two things jumping out: 1) `tool_args` is a string containing JSON (not an object), and there are unescaped quotes around O'Connor (double quotes next to a single quote) plus a trailing comma. 2) Do you have a failing request id?

bob_acme: Request id from headers: rdx-req-20260317-88a7. Sample error from API: `400 Malformed tool args: unexpected token at position 38`

alice_support: Tracing that id now. FYI the upstream schema requires `tool_args` to be a JSON object (not a JSON-encoded string) when calling functions/tools — passing a string will cause our schema validator to attempt a parse and fail on invalid quoting.

erin_supportlead: @alice_support thanks for triage. @dmitri_engineer can you weigh in on whether we should be more lenient server-side or return clearer error text? Customer reports this just started after a small SDK change on their side. :eyes:

dmitri_engineer: @erin_supportlead @alice_support quick read — parsing failure is expected if we try to JSON.parse the string and it contains unescaped quotes/trailing commas. Two options: 1) immediate: change error to include "tool_args must be an object" and echo the offending substring, 2) longer: accept JSON strings and attempt a safe parse with strict failures flagged. Prefer 1 for now to avoid silent coercion.

carol_oncall: can you share the server log snippet for rdx-req-20260317-88a7?

alice_support: Pasted from logs (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-17T09:12:45.312Z] rdx-req-20260317-88a7 ERROR validation: tool_schema.parse_error at pos 38: Unexpected token '"'\npayload: ..."tool_args":"{\"user_id\": \"12345\", \"filter\": \"name:\"O'Connor\"\",}"...
```

alice_support: Also added the customer's SDK snippet — they build `tool_args` by string interpolation which led to unescaped double quotes when a name contains a quote.

dmitri_engineer: Repro locally with their exact string — confirmed. If `tool_args` is sent as a JSON object instead of a quoted string it works: `"tool_args": {"user_id":"12345","filter":"name:\"O'Connor\""}`. But note the inner quote still needs escaping in JSON.

bob_acme: We generate the payload in Ruby by doing `tool_args = params.to_json` then interpolating into a bigger JSON string — looks like a double-encoding bug on our end.

alice_support: Suggested immediate workaround to customer: stop building the outer JSON by hand; use SDK call that accepts a native object for tool args or send `tool_args` as a JSON object value. Example curl that works: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/respond \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{\n   "model": "gpt-4o-mini",\n   "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Find user"}],\n   "function_call": {"name":"lookup_user"},\n   "tool_args": {"user_id":"12345","filter":"name:\\"O\\'Connor\\""}\n }'
```

alice_support: Sent workaround to customer; they confirmed reduced error rate but asked for clearer server errors so their telemetry can alert faster.

erin_supportlead: @dmitri_engineer can you do the quick error-text change and a docs note? Customer impact low but regression from their SDK change caused noise in their system.

dmitri_engineer: Will do. I'll add a validation message change in parser to return `422 - tool_args must be an object or a valid JSON string` with the offending snippet. Will also add a doc blurb in "Function & Tool Calling" about not double-encoding and examples in Ruby/Python/JS.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for change rdx/parser/validation-improve (sha: abc123)

dmitri_engineer: Patch merged, canary looks good, rolling to prod now.

deploy-bot: Rollout complete to 80% of traffic; monitoring 5m... :thumbsup:

alice_support: Let me know when prod roll is done and I'll ask customer to re-run bulk job.

dmitri_engineer: Done — full rollout complete. Release note: improved parser error -> `422: tool_args invalid: expected object or valid JSON string (near: "name:\"O'Connor\"")`. Also added an SDK lint rule to warn on stringified `tool_args`.

bob_acme: Confirmed — their bulk job completed successfully after we removed double-encoding. Thanks everyone, saved us from a big outage in production runs. :raised_hands:

erin_supportlead: Closing loop — docs updated, support KB created, added test case to our parser tests to catch trailing-comma & unescaped-quote cases. Marking resolved.

alice_support: I'll attach KB link in the ticket and advise they upgrade to latest SDK or stop manual string interpolation.

bob_acme: Appreciate the quick turnaround.
